lessonPlan.title: Farm Animals
lessonPlan.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will explore farm life through animal sounds, care routines, sensory bins, books, songs, and dramatic play. Children will name farm animals, describe what they provide, and practice caring for living things.
lessonPlan.objectives:
Name common farm animals and their sounds
Describe products animals provide such as milk and eggs
Practice caring routines for animals
Use farm vocabulary in songs and play
Sort and classify farm animals
Build empathy for animal care
lessonPlan.weeklyMaterials:
Plastic farm animals
Barn playset or cardboard barn
Hay or straw sensory filler
Mud play dough
Farm picture books
Egg cartons (empty)
Buckets and brushes
Farm animal puzzles
Market baskets
Farm sound cards
lessonPlan.vocabularyWords:
farm
barn
cow
pig
chicken
horse
sheep
hay
milk
egg
harvest
farmer
lessonPlan.observationOpportunities: Observe animal naming, sound imitation, caring play, sorting skills, and use of farm vocabulary.
lessonPlan.adaptations: Use real photos alongside toy animals. Supervise sensory bins closely. Offer single-animal focus for overwhelmed children.
lessonPlan.familyConnection: Visit a farmers market or watch farm animals online with family. Discuss foods that come from farms.

items.title: Farm Animal Discovery Basket
items.objective: Explore farm animals and textures in a basket.
items.description: Preschoolers touch animals, hay, and eggs while naming farm creatures.
items.materials: Farm animals, hay, fabric eggs, basket
items.setup: Fill basket with safe farm items.
items.steps:
1. Reach into basket and choose item.
2. Name animal or object.
3. Describe how it feels.
4. Match animal to sound card.
5. Return items gently.
items.observationOpportunities:
Names animals
Imitates sounds
Handles materials gently
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Old MacDonald Sing Along
items.objective: Sing and act out farm animal verses.
items.description: Preschoolers choose animals for Old MacDonald verses with motions.
items.materials: Farm animal props, music or voice
items.setup: Sit in circle with animal props in center.
items.steps:
1. Sing opening verse together.
2. Child picks animal for next verse.
3. Everyone makes animal sound and motion.
4. Continue until many animals sung.
5. Bow and clap for farmers.
items.teacherRole: Pause for children to choose animals.
items.observationOpportunities:
Sings along
Makes animal sound
Takes turn choosing
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Farm Animal Walk
items.objective: Move like farm animals across the room.
items.description: Preschoolers gallop like horses, waddle like ducks, and stomp like cows.
items.steps:
1. Pick animal card.
2. Move like that animal across room.
3. Freeze when music stops.
4. Switch to new animal.
5. Rest with farmer stretch.
items.observationOpportunities:
Imitates animal movement
Freezes on cue
Stays safe in space
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Animal Sorting Center
items.objective: Sort animals by farm habitat or product.
items.description: Preschoolers sort animals into barn, pond, and field mats.
items.setup: Prepare mats labeled barn, pond, field.
items.steps:
1. Pick animal figure.
2. Discuss habitat.
3. Place on correct mat.
4. Count animals on each mat.
5. Resort when new animals added.
items.observationOpportunities:
Sorts logically
States habitat reason
Counts groups
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Muddy Pig Sensory Bin

items.description: Preschoolers roll pigs in brown play dough mud and describe texture.

items.title: Farmer's Market Dramatic Play
items.objective: Buy and sell farm goods at a market stand.

items.title: Milking the Cow Fine Motor
items.objective: Squeeze water from glove udder into bucket.
items.description: Preschoolers practice squeezing a glove filled with water mimicking milking.
items.materials: Rubber glove with pinholes, water, bucket, towel
items.steps:
1. Demonstrate gentle squeeze.
2. Child squeezes glove fingers.
3. Watch water drip to bucket.
4. Discuss milk from cows.
5. Dry area and hands.
items.observationOpportunities:
Squeezes with control
Understands milk source
Follows cleanup

items.title: Egg Carton Counting
items.objective: Place correct number of eggs in carton sections.
items.description: Preschoolers count plastic eggs into carton cups labeled with numerals.
items.materials: Empty egg carton, plastic eggs, numeral labels
items.steps:

2. Place matching number of eggs.

4. Empty and try new numerals.

Counts accurately
Matches numeral to quantity
Self-corrects

teacherTips: Set the discovery basket at child height before circle.
Name one animal aloud as each child chooses an item.
observationPrompts: Does the child name or gesture toward a familiar animal?
Do they take turns choosing from the basket?

teacherTips: Offer a dry towel station beside the muddy pig bin.
Keep the mud thick enough to scoop, not pour.
observationPrompts: Uses describing words like sticky or soft?

teacherTips: Label dramatic-play shelves so children can reset the market.
Model one polite market phrase, then step back.
Pre-count egg cartons so each child has a clear start.
observationPrompts: Self-corrects when an egg is skipped?

teacherTips: Preview bingo sounds once before the game.
Keep rounds short so every child hears a turn.
